findings.body: `selectionValues` returns explicitly filtered dimension values only when the resulting set has exactly one member. Consequently, an `in` filter selecting multiple cost centers, GLs, or other grouped dimensions produces no seed coordinates. If one selected coordinate has no facts, `completeMonthlyCoordinates` never creates its monthly gap rows, so the response silently omits part of the requested scope. Return every explicitly selected value here; the existing Cartesian-product logic can then materialize the required gaps. This is new evidence against the coordinator ruling that every explicitly selected coordinate is materialized.

findings.body: The missing-closing-month assertion calls only `sumClosingMonthRollover` and accepts its raw zero result. It never exercises `FinancialQueryRepository`/`resultValues`, where the `closingLoaded` guard must convert an absent closing month into the required not-loaded state instead of exposing a zero balance. Removing or breaking that guard would leave this test passing, so the required missing-closing-month behavior lacks a test through the real entry point.
